fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides so responders can identify it without delay during low-visibility conditions.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and enough width for emergency vehicles to pass through.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure so fire and emergency vehicles can reposition without backing out to the road.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to create open space between plant material and the buildings.
• Thin dense vegetation between the access drive and the structures so responders on foot can move directly between them without obstruction.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of overgrown plantings so responders can move quickly between buildings.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and any gates or obstacles along the access drive.
• Keep any gates along the access drive unlocked or equipped with a lock box so responders are not delayed reaching the structures.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Ground Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles from around the structure and any nearby outbuildings.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees closest to the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the building.
• Clear ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure to reduce the path fire can take from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Thin shrubs in the brush area closest to the structure to reduce the concentration of burnable material near the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, shrubs, and debris along its full length.
• Remove shrubs and woody debris from the limited rear access area to allow movement around the back of the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation along the edges of the driveway and access route to maintain open, passable lanes.
• Move any stored woody debris, brush piles, or cut vegetation away from the structure and outbuildings.
• Thin scattered shrubs between the brush area and the structure to increase separation between dense vegetation and the building.
